rules.title: tdd-pi artifact present and tracked
rules.source: v3 PLAN §11 D6–D10 — the plugin boundary; the tdd-pi plugin's tdd.json is the test-discipline evidence a repo commits
rules.lesson: A plugin is known by its artifact, not by its data: baseline asks whether tdd.json is there and whether git tracks it, and never opens it — the file's schema, its covers[] and its source commit are tdd-pi's own business (D7).
rules.rationale: One always-on WARN per plugin (D8): absence is named once, with the install command, and never changes the exit code. When the artifact is present the one further question is git's (D9): tdd.json is committed evidence, so the default expects it tracked, and a config-vs-git disagreement is the finding. Every WARN leaves .baseline/log/PLUG-01.log recording the path inspected, the config values used and git's answer (D10).
rules.fix: Install the plugin and run it once so tdd.json lands at the repo root (the install command in the finding is a placeholder for the plugin's own instructions), then commit tdd.json. A different location or gitignore policy is declared in baseline.config.json: {"plugins": {"tdd-pi": {"path": "tools/tdd.json", "ignored": false}}}.

rules.title: graphify graph present and gitignored
rules.source: v3 PLAN §11 D6–D10 — the plugin boundary; graphify's graphify-out/ is a derived knowledge graph, rebuilt from the tree
rules.lesson: The graph is a plugin artifact: the only questions baseline asks are whether graphify-out/ is there, how old it is, and whether git ignores it. `Built from commit:` is a line in a file graphify owns, and reading it would make the verdict depend on the plugin's format (D7).
rules.rationale: One always-on WARN per plugin (D8): an absent graph is named once, with the install command, and never changes the exit code. When present, the one further question is git's (D9): a derived store belongs in .gitignore, so the default expects it ignored, and a tracked graphify-out/ is the finding (config says ignored, git says tracked). Every WARN leaves .baseline/log/PLUG-02.log recording the path inspected, the config values used and git's answer (D10).
rules.fix: Install the plugin and build the graph so graphify-out/ exists (the install command in the finding is a placeholder for the plugin's own instructions), and add graphify-out/ to .gitignore. A different location or gitignore policy is declared in baseline.config.json: {"plugins": {"graphify": {"path": "graphify-out", "ignored": true}}}.

rules.title: okf-rag bundle present
rules.source: v3 PLAN §11 D6–D10 — the plugin boundary; okf-rag's bundle is the concept store `baseline explain` addresses by concept id, at $BASELINE_OKF_BUNDLE
rules.lesson: The bundle is addressed by path or env and never read during check: no verdict depends on a retrieval (§1 V3), and the audit `explain --audit` resolves by filename alone. Presence, kind, age and git state are the whole question (D7).
rules.rationale: One always-on WARN per plugin (D8): an unset or missing bundle is named once, with the install command, and never changes the exit code. The bundle usually lives outside the repo, and a path outside the repo is not asked the gitignore question at all (D9); a bundle kept inside the repo is a derived store, so the default expects it ignored. Every WARN leaves .baseline/log/PLUG-03.log recording the path inspected, the config values used and git's answer (D10).
rules.fix: Install the plugin (the install command in the finding is a placeholder for the plugin's own instructions), export BASELINE_OKF_BUNDLE=<dir> pointing at its bundle, or declare the path in baseline.config.json: {"plugins": {"okf-rag": {"path": "/abs/path/to/bundle", "ignored": true}}}. `baseline gen okf-concepts` stages the per-rule concepts the bundle is built from.
